headline: The breath
of the wok.
hero.text: Carbon steel, a flame at full height, and a kitchen that cooks to the second. Tuesday to Sunday, from five.
hero.caption: Wok-seared beef, broccoli, red chili

image.alt: A carbon steel wok on a roaring burner: sliced beef, broccoli and red chili in the pan under a tall flare of orange flame, with steam rising into a dark kitchen.

process.heading: Heat is the ingredient.
process.body: Wok hei, the breath of the wok, is the smoky, singed sweetness that only comes from food moving fast over a very hot flame. Four things make it, and we cook around all of them.

steps.name: Fire
steps.text: A burner kept at full height, so the pan never has time to cool.

steps.name: Steam
steps.text: Wine and stock flash at the wall of the wok and lift the aroma into the dish.

steps.name: Texture
steps.text: Small cuts, dry ingredients, and a toss that never stops. Crisp stays crisp.

steps.name: The plate
steps.text: Out of the wok and onto jade or slate within seconds, while it is still singing.

meta.title: Our story
meta.description: The story of Jade & Ember, a fictional modern Chinese kitchen built around one very hot wok.

story.h1: A small kitchen, one very hot wok.

image.alt: Three stacked jade-green celadon bowls beside a bowl of steamed white rice on a matte black plate, on a slate board.

story.caption: Celadon rice bowls, stacked on the pass.
paragraphs: Jade & Ember began as a question about a single flame: what if a dining room felt like standing beside a wok at full heat, without the noise or the smoke?

The room is charcoal and slate, lit low, with celadon bowls stacked on the pass. The kitchen cooks Cantonese and Sichuan dishes with a lighter hand, and the menu stays short so every dish gets its turn at the fire.
Jade for the bowls, ember for the flame. The name is the whole palette.
